properties.text: THE THIN LENS -- a physics plate drawn by one Figure node.  Spin the wheel over the two knobs: OBJECT DISTANCE u slides the black arrow along the axis; FOCAL LENGTH f moves the two focal points F and F′ and the 2F marks.  The three rays every textbook draws leave the tip of the object -- red parallel to the axis and then through F′, green straight through the centre, blue through F and then parallel -- and the purple image is drawn where they actually cross, from 1/u + 1/v = 1/f worked out in the program's own lines.  Wind u in from the far left: past 2F the image is smaller than the object (a camera), between 2F and F it is larger (a projector), at F the rays leave parallel and there is no image at all (a searchlight), and inside F they spread apart and only their dashed extensions back through the lens meet -- a virtual, upright image on the object's own side (a magnifying glass).  One lens, and the lower-right line of the readout says which instrument it is.

properties.program:
# THE THIN LENS
#
# Two knobs: how far the OBJECT stands from the lens (u) and the
# lens's FOCAL LENGTH (f).  The three construction rays every
# textbook draws leave the tip of the object, and the image is
# drawn where they actually cross.  Wind u in through 2f and f and
# the image grows, runs off to infinity, and comes back on the
# wrong side the right way up -- a camera, a projector and a
# magnifying glass, one lens.

view -86, -81, 86, 48
align "centre", "middle"

# The plate, in centimetres; the readout lives in the band below it.
XL = -84
XR =  84
YT =  46
YB = -50
h  =  10

# ==================================================================
#  THE PHYSICS, in two lines: 1/u + 1/v = 1/f, and m = -v/u.
#  v > 0 is a real image behind the lens, v < 0 a virtual one in
#  front of it.  At u = f exactly v is infinite and everything that
#  mentions it is simply not drawn (80.10).
# ==================================================================
v  = u * f / (u - f)
m  = -v / u
hi = m * h

# --- the axis, the focal points and the lens plane ----------------
color "#202020"
width 0.6
line XL, 0, XR, 0

line 0, YB, 0, YT  with color "#9aa6ab", width 0.45, dash "dot"

# A biconvex lens, 60 tall and 6 thick; the construction treats it as
# the thin plane through its middle, which is why the dotted line goes
# on past its ends -- a ray may meet the plane higher than the glass.
# Each face is a parabola: one curve segment whose control points lie
# two thirds of the way from its ends to (6, 0), where the tangents at
# the lens's tips cross.
width 0.5
with color "#6f8f9c", fill "#dbe6ea"
    curve 0, 30,   4, 10,   4, -10,   0, -30,
          -4, -10,   -4, 10,   0, 30
end

color "#202020"
with fill "#202020"
    circle -f, 0, 0.9
    circle  f, 0, 0.9
end
width 0.5
line -2 * f, -1.4, -2 * f, 1.4
line  2 * f, -1.4,  2 * f, 1.4
width 0.25
line -2 * f, -1.4, -2 * f, -7.6
line  2 * f, -1.4,  2 * f, -7.6

font 5
align "centre", "top"
text -f,     -2.3, "F"
text  f,     -2.5, "F′"
text -2 * f, -8.2, "2F"
text  2 * f, -8.2, "2F′"

# ==================================================================
#  THE THREE RAYS, each from the tip of the object (-u, h).
#  Every segment is cut where it would leave the plate, so a ray
#  that runs off the top never paints across the readout.
# ==================================================================
# Each ray's head points the way the light goes, its tip halfway along.
wr = 0.7
arrowhead 3.3, 3.1

# (1) PARALLEL to the axis, then bent through F'.
color "#b03a2e"
width wr
s1 = -h / f
x1 = min(XR, (YB - h) / s1)
path -u, h, 0, h, x1, h + s1 * x1
head -u, h, -0.5 * u, h

# (2) through the CENTRE, undeviated.
color "#2e7d4f"
s2 = -h / u
x2 = min(XR, YB / s2)
line -u, h, x2, s2 * x2
head -u, h, -0.5 * u, 0.5 * h

# (3) through F, then leaving PARALLEL.  With the object inside the
# focal length the ray cannot pass F on its way to the tip, so it
# starts there instead: the start is whichever is further out.
color "#3a5a9b"
y3 = -h * f / (u - f)
s3 = (y3 - h) / u
xs = -max(u, f)
Y3 = YB + (YT - YB) * (s3 > 0)
xe = min(0, -u + (Y3 - h) / s3)
line xs, h + s3 * (xs + u), xe, h + s3 * (xe + u)
xm = 0.5 * (xs + xe)
head xs, h + s3 * (xs + u), xm, h + s3 * (xm + u)
y3on = (y3 < YT) * (y3 > YB)
if y3on
    line 0, y3, XR, y3
end

# --- a virtual image: the rays diverge, and only their dashed
# extensions BACK through the lens meet, so these three lines exist
# only on the magnifying-glass side of f.
if v < 0
    with width 0.45, dash "dash", 0.6
        xb = max(v, max(XL, f * (1 - YT / h)))
        line 0, h, xb, h + s1 * xb  with color "#b03a2e"
        xb = max(v, max(XL, YT / s2))
        line -u, h, xb, s2 * xb  with color "#2e7d4f"
        if y3on
            xb = max(v, XL)
            line 0, y3, xb, y3  with color "#3a5a9b"
        end
    end
end

# ==================================================================
#  THE OBJECT AND ITS IMAGE
# ==================================================================
color "#202020"
width 1.3
arrowhead 4.4, 4.4
arrow -u, 0, -u, h

# The image arrow only where it fits on the plate; the readout still
# gives the number when it does not.
onp = (v > XL) * (v < XR) * (hi > YB) * (hi < YT)

color "#7a3d8c"
if onp * (v > 0)
    arrow v, 0, v, hi
elseif onp * (v < 0)
    # the virtual image is a ghost: thin and dashed, no ink behind it
    arrow v, 0, v, hi  with width 0.8, dash "dash", 0.6, arrowhead 3.7, 3.7
end

# ==================================================================
#  THE READOUT, in the band below the plate
# ==================================================================
line XL + 2, -54, XR - 2, -54  with color "#9aa6ab", width 0.4

color "#202020"
text 82, 46, "The thin lens"  with font 6.6, align "right", "top"

font 5.4
align "left", "top"
text -82, -57,   "u = %.1f cm    f = %.1f cm", u, f
if abs(u / f - 1) > 0.02
    text -82, -64.5, "1/v = 1/f − 1/u → v = %.1f cm", v
    text -82, -72,   "m = −v/u = %.2f", m
else
    text -82, -64.5, "1/v = 1/f − 1/u = %.0f → v → ∞", abs(1 / f - 1 / u)
end

# What kind of image, and what the lens is FOR at that distance.
r = u / f
color "#7a3d8c"
if r > 2.05
    text 0, -57, "u = %.2f f: CAMERA", r
elseif abs(r - 2) <= 0.05
    text 0, -57, "u = %.2f f: COPIER", r
elseif (r > 1.02) * (r < 1.95)
    text 0, -57, "u = %.2f f: PROJECTOR", r
elseif abs(r - 1) <= 0.02
    text 0, -57, "u = %.2f f: SEARCHLIGHT", r
elseif r < 0.98
    text 0, -57, "u = %.2f f: MAGNIFYING GLASS", r
end

color "#202020"
if abs(r - 1) <= 0.02
    text 0, -64.5, "no image: rays leave at %.1f°", degrees(atan(h / u))
elseif v > 0
    text 0, -64.5, "real, inverted, %.2f× as tall", -m
elseif v < 0
    text 0, -64.5, "virtual, upright, %.2f× as tall", m
end
